t: There's no mansion here now. This is the site of Montagu House, a late seventeenth century mansion on Great Russell Street, which became the first home of the British Museum. The first house burned down in 1686, and the rebuilt one was sold to the Museum in 1759. It was demolished in the 1840s to make way for the larger building you see today. Robert Hooke, the scientist and architect, designed it, and Ralph Montagu, the first Duke of Montagu, a courtier, diplomat and politician, lived here.
